message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – key physical and chemical properties:

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2H), Tritium (^3H) |
| **Standard atomic weight** | ~1.008 u (weighted average of isotopes) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ/mol) |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ/mol) |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ/mol) |
| **Boiling point (at 1 atm)** | –252.87 °C (20.44 K) |
| **Melting point (at 1 atm)** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g/L (≈0.0000899 kg/m³) |
| **Molecular form** | Diatomic gas (H₂) under normal conditions |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ/mol |
| **Acidity/basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (forming H⁺) or base (forming H⁻) depending on context; forms hydrides with metals (e.g., NaH, CaH₂). |
| **Oxidation states** | +1 (as proton H⁺), –1 (as hydride H⁻); also +2 in compounds like H₂O₂ (hydroperoxide). |
| **Common allotropes** | Molecular hydrogen (H₂), atomic hydrogen (in plasma or high‑temperature environments). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – classic hydrogen emission spectrum. |
| **Reactivity** | Combines with oxygen to form water (exothermic combustion). Forms hydrides with many elements; reacts with halogens to give hydrogen halides (HF, HCl, HBr, HI). |
| **Uses** | Fuel (rocket propellant, fuel cells), reducing agent in metallurgy, laboratory standard for calibration, production of ammonia (Haber process). |

These values capture the most frequently cited characteristics of hydrogen in chemistry and physics contexts.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are the different properties of Hydrogen?" They want properties of hydrogen. We can provide general properties: atomic number, symbol, mass, electronegativity, ionization energy, electron affinity, boiling point, melting point, density, etc. Also chemical properties: diatomic molecule H2, forms hydrides, acidity, basicity, etc. But maybe they want a list of properties. We should answer concisely but comprehensively. No tool needed.
